- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; adjust downward by 3–8% for next 3–7 days, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); cap forecast at +5–7% above recent peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model lags; forecast should rise 2–4 days ahead of true trend.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate if sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.5); add 2–5% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+1.00” followed by “-1.00”, model overreacts; dampen forecast by 3–6% for next 5 days.
